title: Burke and Wills expedition
summary: The Victorian Exploring Expedition, organised by the Royal Society of Victoria, left Melbourne on 20 August 1860 before a crowd of fifteen thousand. From a depot at Menindee and a camp at Cooper's Creek, Burke, Wills, King and Gray set out north on 16 December and reached the Gulf of Carpentaria in February 1861. Gray died on 17 April; Burke and Wills died in late June. King alone survived, helped by Aboriginal people.

uncertainty.note: Dates are from EBSCO; the Australian Museum dates the arrival back at the Cooper's Creek camp to 21 April 1861.

reviewer_note: Dates rest on EBSCO alone (National Museum of Australia and Museums Victoria pages returned 403). Australian Museum: organised by the Royal Society of Victoria, Burke dashed north with Wills, King and Gray; Gray's death attributed to short provisions, scurvy, weather and hostile Aboriginals; King helped by Aboriginals. Burke & Wills Web: seven men died; of the four who reached the north coast, King alone survived. No opened page names the Yandruwandha or other Aboriginal nations; add that from a museum or community source on expansion. The Cooper's Creek waypoint is an Innamincka point with 100 km record uncertainty. Waypoint years are day-of-year fractions.

beats.caption: The expedition leaves Royal Park, Melbourne, on 20 August 1860 before a crowd of about fifteen thousand.
Burke, Wills, King and Gray leave Cooper's Creek on 16 December and reach the gulf on the Little Bynoe River in February 1861.
Seven men die in all; John King survives, nursed by Aboriginal people until a search party finds him on 15 September 1861.
